title: Exceptional inverse image of a smooth morphism commutes with extension of coefficients
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ has characteristic $p>0$, $\ell\ne p$ is prime, and $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix its coefficient-independent compactification. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings, each annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Write $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ for complexes of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $R_T$ with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Use derived coefficient extension $K_B=K\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], the constructible adjunctions $Rf_{!,R}\dashv f_R^!$ for $R=A,B$ [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], and the canonical compact-support comparison $b$ [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. For a common annihilator $N=\ell^n$ of $A,B$, the Tate line is the inverse image from the etale site of $\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$; write $K(d)=K\otimes^L_R R_T(1)^{\otimes d}$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist].

For
$K\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ let

$$
c_{A,B}(K):(f_A^!K)_B\longrightarrow f_B^!(K_B)\quad\text{in }\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)
$$

be the unique morphism (the transpose under $Rf_{!,B}\dashv f_B^!$) satisfying

$$
\varepsilon_B(K_B)\circ Rf_{!,B}\bigl(c_{A,B}(K)\bigr)
=(\varepsilon_A(K))_B\circ b(f_A^!K)^{-1}.
$$

Then $c_{A,B}(K)$ is natural in $K$ and is an isomorphism. On a coordinate
chart $f|_U=p_d\circ e$ (with $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ étale and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is the chart inclusion, where
$j^*f_A^!\simeq e^*p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$ is the counit-preserving identification for the chart adjunction whose counit is summation over the fibres of $e$ followed by the affine-space counit of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], transported from the etale site) it is the canonical isomorphism
$(e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d])_B\simeq e^*p_d^*(K_B)(d)[2d]$.

proof.text: Put $T_X=(-)_B$, $T_Y=(-)_B$, $F_R=Rf_{!,R}$ and $G_R=f_R^!$. By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](1),(2), $T_X,T_Y$ preserve the indicated categories. By [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], $F_R\dashv G_R$ is an adjunction on them. Applying [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] to $G_AK$ gives the natural isomorphism $b(G_AK):T_YF_AG_AK\to F_BT_XG_AK$. Thus $\tau_K=T_Y(\varepsilon_A(K))b(G_AK)^{-1}$ is a well-typed map $F_BT_XG_AK\to T_YK$, with no flatness requirement on $B$ over $A$.

Under the adjunction of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], define $c_K$ to be the transpose of $\tau_K$. The inverse transpose of $h:T_XG_AK\to G_BT_YK$ is $\varepsilon_B(T_YK)F_B(h)$. Hence its counit identity is exactly the displayed identity in the statement, and this identity determines $c_K$ uniquely. For $u:K\to L$, naturality of $b$ [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] and of $\varepsilon_A$ gives $T_Y(u)\tau_K=\tau_LF_BT_XG_A(u)$. Naturality of $\varepsilon_B$ identifies the left side with the inverse transpose of $G_BT_Y(u)c_K$ and the right side with the inverse transpose of $c_LT_XG_A(u)$. Injectivity of the hom bijection proves naturality of $c$.

source.place: Existence, uniqueness, naturality: transpose and its naturality

proof.text:
We perform the finite-coefficient chart calculation on ordinary etale sites and transport it, retaining the counits. This is legitimate for arbitrary finite $R=A,B$, rather than only DVR quotient rings: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] gives bounded constructible etale origin, [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] gives full faithfulness there, so they identify all Hom sets between these objects. The coefficient and chart pullbacks preserve derived tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and comparison inverse image is exact and carries constant rings to constant rings [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. In particular coefficient extension and the twist-and-shift chart functors are transported to the same functors on the pro-etale side. To check the finite-Tor subcategory here, test a bounded etale complex $L$ against etale module sheaves $M$: monoidality gives $
u^*(L\otimes^L_R M)=
u^*L\otimes^L_R
u^*M$. Exactness identifies cohomology even for the possibly unbounded tensor complex; full faithfulness on degree-zero sheaves reflects whether each such cohomology sheaf is zero. Thus finite Tor amplitude of $
u^*L$ implies the etale finite Tor bound. All schemes here are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over the Noetherian field $k$. Choose Tor bounds $a\leq b$ (enlarging the interval if necessary). By [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible], choose a bounded termwise-flat constructible etale representative in $[a,b]$. Its derived inverse image has flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and its tensor with the locally free Tate line is still termwise flat by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. For the explicit chart functor its inverse image, invertible Tate line and shift preserve finite Tor amplitude directly; its pro-etale output is the displayed twist of the pullback of $K$. Thus this transport restricts to the constructible finite-Tor objects used here, and does not identify the whole unbounded etale and pro-etale categories. For clarity the needed adjunction transfer is formal, rather than an application of an unspecified admissibility hypothesis. Write $F_R^{\mathrm{et}}\dashv H_R^{\mathrm{et}}$ for the chart adjunction constructed in Steps 6–8. For etale objects $L,N$ in the finite-Tor constructible categories, the equivalence just checked and the specified site comparison give
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(F_R
u_X^*L,
u_Y^*N)
\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(
u_Y^*F_R^{\mathrm{et}}L,
u_Y^*N)
\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F_R^{\mathrm{et}}L,N)
\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(L,H_R^{\mathrm{et}}N)
\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(
u_X^*L,
u_X^*H_R^{\mathrm{et}}N).
$$
The first bijection is precomposition with $c_{f,R}$; hence the counit is $
u_Y^*(\epsilon_R^{\mathrm{et}})c_{f,R}^{-1}$. Counit-preserving uniqueness identifies this right adjoint with the constructible right adjoint of the chart map (for the chart $g$ of Step 8, with $G_{g,R}\simeq j^*G_R$ there). This derives the formal counit formula described in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer] for every finite $R$ here; no ambient Brown-adjoint or additional admissibility hypothesis is used. The first displayed square of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], with $\delta_T:T_T
u_T^*\simeq
u_T^*T_T^{\mathrm{et}}$, states exactly $F_{f,B}(\delta_X)\circ b_f\circ T_Y(c_{f,A})=c_{f,B}\circ
u_Y^*( eta_f^{\mathrm{et}})\circ\delta_Y$. Substitute the transported counit $
u_Y^*(\epsilon_R^{\mathrm{et}})c_{f,R}^{-1}$ just derived into the ordinary chart counit identity. This square cancels $c_{f,A}$ and $c_{f,B}$ against their inverses; naturality of $\delta_Y$ moves it past $\epsilon_A^{\mathrm{et}}$. The resulting equality is precisely the pro-etale counit identity with the named $b_f$, not a freely chosen isomorphism of its endpoints.

source.place: Charts: finite etale/pro-etale comparison before the calculation

proof.text: For $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ over any base chart in our setting, choose $N=\ell^n$ annihilating both rings and put $R_0=\mathbf Z/N$. The bases and projective lines are Noetherian and $N$ is invertible; Noetherianity follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], for $R=A,B$ the splitting $s_R:R_S(1)[2]\oplus R_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*R_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]$ has components the shifted unit and the scalar-extended Kummer class $h_R$. More precisely, the cited statement defines $h_R$ by first taking the Kummer class over $R_0$, extending scalars to $R$ on $\mathbf P^1_S$, and then applying inverse-image/direct-image adjunction. Write $H_0:(R_0)_{\mathbf P^1_S}\to(R_0)_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]$ for that Kummer morphism. Then $H_R=H_0\otimes^L_{R_0}R$ has adjunct $h_R$. Derived tensor associativity gives $(H_0\otimes^L_{R_0}A)\otimes^L_AB=H_0\otimes^L_{R_0}B$, with the canonical identifications of both endpoints; hence $(H_A)_B=H_B$. Step 5 checks the corresponding direct-image equality with the named coefficient map by transposition.

source.place: Charts: common exponent and scalar-extended Kummer class

proof.text:
On the ordinary etale site put $b_q=\beta_q^{\mathrm{et}}$, the proper comparison explicitly defined and asserted invertible in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], evaluated on $A_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]$. The source twist is locally free of rank one by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. Thus its derived scalar extension is ordinary tensor and is canonically $B_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]$: on an etale trivialization the map is $A\otimes_A B\to B$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, and these maps respect the transition units of $\mu_N$. On the two components of the splitting of Step 4 the comparison sends the unit to the unit and $(h_A)_B$ to $h_B$. For the unit this follows from the defining counit-transpose projection map: its composite with the pullback/direct-image unit is the coefficient-extended unit, by the adjunction triangle identity; for the second component, take the inverse transpose of $b_q(h_A)_B$ under $q_B^*\dashv Rq_{*,B}$. The defining counit identity for $b_q$ and naturality give $(\epsilon_{q,*,A}\,q_A^*h_A)_B=(H_A)_B=H_B$, where $\epsilon_{q,*,A}$ is the ordinary pullback/direct-image counit, not the exceptional counit. The inverse transpose of $h_B$ is also $H_B$ by definition; injectivity of this hom bijection gives $b_q(h_A)_B=h_B$. Thus $b_q(s_A)_B=s_B$. By [def-amb-p1-trace], $t_{q,R}=\operatorname{pr}_2s_R^{-1}$. Multiplying the preceding equality by inverses gives
$$t_{q,B}\,b_q=(t_{q,A})_B.$$
Indeed both composites with $(s_A)_B$ are the projection onto the second summand. This is a two-component calculation with an invertible splitting, not an extra lemma asserting the desired exceptional comparison.

source.place: Charts: scalar extension of the projective-line splitting and trace

proof.text:
The actual projective-line counit is $\epsilon_{q,R,K}=(1_K\otimes t_{q,R})\pi_R^{-1}$ with the tensor unit constraint, by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] and [def-amb-p1-trace]. Put $L_R=R_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]$ and $F_R=Rq_{*,R}$, so $G_{q,R}K=q_R^*K\otimes_R^L L_R$. The canonical tensor/pullback comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Apply the square of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the ringed-topos square with scheme maps $q,q$ and coefficient change $A\to B$. After its canonical tensor and symmetry identifications, the square says exactly
$$
F_B(a_{q,K})\,b_q(G_{q,A}K)\,(\pi_A)_B
=\pi_B\,(1_{K_B}\otimes b_q(L_A)),
$$
where $a_{q,K}:(q^*K(1)[2])_B\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*(K_B)(1)[2]$. Both sides start at $K_B\otimes_B^L(F_AL_A)_B$ and end at $F_BG_{q,B}(K_B)$. Compose with $\epsilon_{q,B,K_B}=(1\otimes t_{q,B})\pi_B^{-1}$. The right side becomes $1_{K_B}\otimes(t_{q,B}b_q(L_A))=1_{K_B}\otimes(t_{q,A})_B$ by Step 5; this is $(\epsilon_{q,A,K})_B(\pi_A)_B$. Since $(\pi_A)_B$ and $b_q(G_{q,A}K)$ are isomorphisms, cancellation gives
$$
(\epsilon_{q,A,K})_B\,b_q(G_{q,A}K)^{-1}
=\epsilon_{q,B,K_B}\,Rq_{*,B}(a_{q,K}).
$$
Thus the actual counit at every $K$ has the required coefficient identity. This argument uses no flatness of $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Charts: projective-line counit at an arbitrary complex

proof.text:
For an open immersion $j$ and for a separated etale chart map $e$, coefficient extension commutes with their exact sum-extension functors and their counits. For $e$ use [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] and [lem-amb-etale-sum-stalks]: the counit on a fibre is $\bigoplus_x M_x\to M$, $(m_x)\mapsto\sum_xm_x$. Tensoring this map with $b\in B$ gives $\sum_x(m_x\otimes b)$, exactly the $B$-counit. More explicitly, the direct-sum presheaf of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] gives the projection identity $e_!(P\otimes_A e^*N)=e_!P\otimes_A N$ by the balancing formula on each summand. For a K-flat complex $P$ and acyclic $N$, $e^*N$ is acyclic and $e_!(P\otimes_A e^*N)$ is acyclic because both $e^*$ and $e_!$ are exact. Thus $e_!P$ is K-flat; the same summand formula and counit equality hold on complexes before passing to the derived category. The open case is its restriction/extension-by-zero case. No flatness of $B$ is used. The affine-space adjunction of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] is explicitly defined by restricting the projective-line adjunction to $\mathbf A^1$ and composing along the coordinate tower; for $d=0$ it is the identity. Here is the composite-counit calculation from [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. For consecutive adjunctions $F_{1,R}\dashv G_{1,R}$ and $F_{2,R}\dashv G_{2,R}$, let $T_i$ change coefficients in the $i$th category, let $b_i:T_iF_{i,A}\to F_{i,B}T_{i-1}$ be the left-functor comparisons, and let $a_i:T_{i-1}G_{i,A}\to G_{i,B}T_i$ be the canonical chart tensor comparisons. Suppose $\epsilon_{i,B}F_{i,B}(a_i)=T_i(\epsilon_{i,A})b_i(G_{i,A}-)^{-1}$, as proved in Step 6 and for sum extension above. Put $G_{12,R}=G_{1,R}G_{2,R}$, $b_{12}=F_{2,B}(b_1)b_2(F_{1,A}-)$ and $a_{12}=G_{1,B}(a_2)a_1(G_{2,A}-)$. At $K$ the composite-counit formula and naturality of $\epsilon_{1,B}$ give
$$
\epsilon_{12,B}F_{2,B}F_{1,B}(a_{12})
=\epsilon_{2,B}F_{2,B}(a_2)\,
 F_{2,B}\bigl(T_1(\epsilon_{1,A})b_1(G_{12,A}K)^{-1}\bigr).
$$
Apply the coefficient identity for $\epsilon_2$ and then naturality of $b_2$ at $\epsilon_{1,A,G_{2,A}K}$ to obtain
$$
\begin{aligned}
& T_2(\epsilon_{2,A})\,b_2(G_{2,A}K)^{-1}
 F_{2,B}T_1(\epsilon_{1,A})\,F_{2,B}(b_1(G_{12,A}K)^{-1})\\
&=T_2\bigl(\epsilon_{2,A}F_{2,A}(\epsilon_{1,A})\bigr)
 b_2(F_{1,A}G_{12,A}K)^{-1}F_{2,B}(b_1(G_{12,A}K)^{-1})\\
&=T_2(\epsilon_{12,A})b_{12}(G_{12,A}K)^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
$$
This proves the composite coefficient identity. Its identity-adjunction case is $d=0$. Composing the projective-line adjunction with the open-extension adjunction proves it for the affine-line adjunction; composing one further affine-line adjunction with the $d$-coordinate adjunction proves the $d+1$ case. The monoidal pullback and tensor associativity identifications of Step 3 identify $a_{12}$ with the canonical comparison for the combined twist and shift. The coherent identification of the ordered compact-support composite with $Rp_{d!}$ is [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. For its coefficient projection map the same composition equality follows by transposing its definition: the composite direct-image counit is $\epsilon_1 f_1^*(\epsilon_2)$ and tensor associativity makes the two transposes identical. Thus this calculation uses the canonical $b$, rather than choosing a new comparison for composites. The composition and refinement squares of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] apply to these arbitrary finite rings: explicitly $b_{gf}T(\alpha_A)=\alpha_B F_{g,B}(b_f)b_g(F_{f,A}-)$ and $b^{c'}T(\phi_A)=\phi_B b^c$. Thus the ordered composite coefficient map in this counit calculation is the fixed-compactification map after the canonical $\alpha$ identifications; the second square makes that assertion independent of the refining tower. These squares, rather than a comparison theorem restricted to listed coefficient maps, justify cancellation of the intermediate comparisons.

source.place: Charts: affine line, iterated affine space, and etale fibre sums

proof.text:
On a chart $g=fj=p_de$ the composite adjunction of Step 7 has right adjoint $H_{g,R}K=e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d]$ and composite counit, by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the etale adjunction [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. The restriction isomorphism $j^*G_R\simeq G_{g,R}$ of [det-sf-mate-open-restriction] identifies it with this right adjoint by the counit-preserving uniqueness of right adjoints. Apply the coefficient identities of Steps 6–7 and the transport of Step 3. With $a_{g,K}:(H_{g,A}K)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{g,B}(K_B)$ they give precisely
$$ (\epsilon_{g,A,K})_B\,b_g(H_{g,A}K)^{-1}
=\epsilon_{g,B,K_B}\,Rg_{!,B}(a_{g,K}). $$
This constructs the chart adjunction for arbitrary finite $A,B$ from existing general finite-ring projective-line and etale adjunctions; the narrower $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ chart lemma is not applied to an arbitrary finite ring. The left adjoint of this composite is $Rp_{d!}\circ De_{\Sigma!}$; by [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] the identification $c_e:Re_!^c\simeq De_{\Sigma!}$ carries the compact-support adjunction of $e$ to $De_{\Sigma!}\dashv e^*$ with its sum/evaluation counit, so composing with the composition map $\alpha$ identifies the chart left adjoint with $Rg_!$, counits included. The etale normalization square of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] says that under $c_e$ the coefficient map $\beta_e^c$ is the summandwise tensor identification used for $e$ in Step 7. Apply the composition and refinement squares of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] to the compactifications of $e$, $p_d$ and $g=p_de$. They identify the coefficient map used in the composite chart counit with $b_g$ for the chosen compactification. Hence the displayed counit identity uses exactly the map defining the transpose $c_{g,K}$.

source.place: Charts: counit identity for the complete coordinate chart

proof.text:
The comparison $c_K$ restricts to the comparison for $g=fj$. Here is the complete cancellation. Write $J_R=j_{!,R}$, $U_R=j_R^*$, and $v_R:J_RU_R\to1$ for the open counit, and let $a_U:T_UU_A\simeq U_BT_X$ be the restriction/tensor identification. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and [det-sf-mate-open-restriction], the counit for $g$ is $\epsilon_{f,R}\,F_{f,R}(v_R G_{f,R})$. The canonical compact-support comparison is
$$b_g(N)=F_{f,B}(b_j(N))\,b_f(J_AN),$$
as follows by the transpose computation in Step 7. After using $a_U$ to identify $T_UU_AG_AK$ with $U_BT_XG_AK$, the inverse transpose of $U_Bc_K$ under the composite adjunction is
$$\epsilon_{f,B}\,F_{f,B}(v_B G_B T_YK)\,F_{f,B}J_B(U_Bc_K)
=\epsilon_{f,B}\,F_{f,B}(c_K)\,F_{f,B}(v_B T_XG_AK),$$
by naturality of $v_B$. The defining equation of $c_K$ turns this into
$$T_Y\epsilon_{f,A}\;b_f(G_AK)^{-1}\;F_{f,B}(v_B T_XG_AK).$$
Step 7's open-counit scalar equality says
$$v_B T_XG_AK=T_X(v_A G_AK)\,b_j(U_AG_AK)^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $b_f$ now rewrites the preceding inverse transpose as
$$T_Y\epsilon_{f,A}\;T_YF_{f,A}(v_A G_AK)\;b_f(J_AU_AG_AK)^{-1}\;F_{f,B}(b_j(U_AG_AK)^{-1})
=T_Y(\epsilon_{g,A,K})\,b_g(U_AG_AK)^{-1}.$$
This is exactly the inverse transpose defining $c_{g,K}$; hence $j^*c_K=c_{g,K}$. Step 8 says the canonical $a_{g,K}$ has this same inverse transpose, so uniqueness gives $j^*c_K=a_{g,K}$, the required chart identification and an isomorphism. Here the composition square of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] for the pair $(j,f)$, after the $\alpha_A,\alpha_B$ identifications, is exactly the displayed formula $b_g=F_{f,B}(b_j)b_f(J_A-)$. Its refinement square identifies this formula with the comparison for the fixed compactification of $g$, so the final inverse transpose is the named one defining $c_{g,K}$.

source.place: Locality and Charts: identify the restricted transpose

proof.text: Smooth local normal form [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] gives coordinate charts after replacing the base and source by affine neighborhoods. Compose its etale map to $\mathbf A^d_V$ with the open immersion $\mathbf A^d_V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_Y$; this is an etale chart over $Y$. Pure relative dimension fixes its dimension to $d$. The affine neighborhoods cover $X$. They are Noetherian, as are $X,Y$ and their affine spaces, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Open subschemes remain Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so the chart open immersions are quasi-compact and are of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), the etale coordinate map from an affine source to the separated affine-space target is of finite presentation, hence finite type. It is separated: its relative diagonal is the base change of the closed diagonal of its separated $k$-source along $U\times_{\mathbf A^d_Y}U\to U\times_kU$, hence closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Thus all these maps satisfy the hypotheses of the adjunctions used above. Step 9 makes every restriction of $c_K$ an isomorphism. Clause (3) of [det-sf-mate-open-restriction] detects isomorphisms on this open cover, and proves $c_K$ is an isomorphism globally. Only isomorphism detection is used here; no assertion that restriction is faithful on all derived morphisms is needed.

source.place: Locality: cover by charts and detection of isomorphisms
